text:
Rasmus Dahlin's season has been steady rather than loud: 10 points in 14 games, 24 and a half minutes a night, and Buffalo controlling 53.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he is out at five on five. He missed most of a week in October after a nine-minute night against Florida, and he has been back on his usual workload since.

The points are a little behind his talent, not because of bad luck but because the assists have dried up lately: none in his last four games. Our range puts his scoring rate a touch above where it is now, and we project him around 65 points.

What makes him worth watching is the puck. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.2 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 99th percentile among defensemen, carrying the puck in on 42% of his entries. Evolving-Hockey had him 12th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement. The Sabres go as he goes, and right now he is going fine.
headline: Dahlin is quietly doing Dahlin things
